The player's breath is aimed at the edge of a hole; this jet of air starts to vibrate and in turn sets the air column in the tube vibrating. The tube favors the vibrations that “fit” its length, like a swing pushed at the right rhythm: this is resonance.

Opening a hole puts the air in contact with the room sooner: the vibrating column is shorter, the note rises. By blowing harder, without touching the holes, the player makes a harmonic resonate instead of the fundamental: the note jumps higher.
